problem: Normal and data-only website changes need bounded affected-route browser proof without paying for unnecessary full header-menu/broad browser regression, while public-page visibility remains a mandatory safety baseline.
root_cause: The original optimization coupled public visibility and header-menu crawling as one global cost. Current main correctly retains public visibility as a safety baseline while allowing expensive menu/broad browser work to be risk-scoped.
prevention: Keep public-page visibility mandatory for previewed website changes, including fast-fix safety coverage.
Reserve full header-menu readability and broad browser contracts for high-risk changes.
For bounded normal-risk changes, use targeted desktop/mobile affected-route verification plus the mandatory visibility baseline.
Map regulatory data changes to a bounded explicit public-route set instead of defaulting to a generic route.
Do not skip baseline, syntax, static or page-SEO contracts required by the selected lane.
